report:
**Conclusion: The claim is false/unsupported.** Food-grade wax coatings on apples do not cause cancer. Fact-checking organizations and food safety experts consistently find no credible evidence linking these waxes to cancer.

Apples naturally produce their own wax coating, which is washed off during commercial processing; a food-grade wax (typically carnauba, shellac, or similar plant/insect-derived substances) is then reapplied to restore moisture retention and extend shelf life ([mcgill.ca](https://www.mcgill.ca/oss/article/you-asked/why-do-they-spray-wax-apples-0)). These waxes are regulated for food use, and safety assessments of common waxes like carnauba, beeswax, and candelilla have not identified carcinogenic properties, describing them instead in terms of chemical composition and industrial/cosmetic uses rather than cancer risk ([cir-safety.org](https://www.cir-safety.org/sites/default/files/RR_Waxes.pdf)).

The cancer claim appears to stem from viral social media videos rather than scientific research. Fact-checking outlets have specifically investigated and debunked these claims: Vishvas News found a viral video claiming wax-coated apples could be deadly to be "misleading" ([vishvasnews.com](https://www.vishvasnews.com/english/health/fact-check-can-consuming-wax-coated-apples-kill-you-misleading-video-getting-viral/)), and reporting from The Daily Meal notes that "the sources claiming that fruit waxing causes cancer are mainly social media influencers who don't back up their claim with concrete evidence," adding that Snopes' own fact-checking found no known carcinogens in common fruit waxes ([thedailymeal.com](https://www.thedailymeal.com/1231103/should-you-remove-the-wax-coating-on-apples-before-you-take-a-bite/)).

**Bottom line:** Food-grade wax on apples is approved for consumption, has no established link to cancer, and the fear is driven by unsubstantiated viral content rather than scientific evidence. Washing produce before eating remains good general practice but is not specifically necessary to avoid a cancer risk from wax.
